title: Credit-card CVV and, in one path, the full unmasked PAN written to application logs
owner_hint: no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer: Aditya Mandaleeka; component: Ordering.API/
rationale: Two root-cause fixes in CreateOrderAsync: the missing/zero-x-requestid branch now logs only request.GetGenericTypeName() instead of destructuring the raw CreateOrderRequest record (which dumped unmasked PAN + CVV via its generated ToString), and CardSecurityNumber is fully masked (X per char) at the command boundary alongside the existing PAN masking — no downstream sink can emit it.
variants_checked: All {@Command} sinks (LoggingBehavior, TransactionBehavior, ValidatorBehavior, IdentifiedCommandHandler, OrdersApi wrapper) safe once the command is masked at construction; domain layer only stores the CVV; validator Length(3) semantics unchanged by length-preserving masking.
bypass_considered: All card-value variations, malformed CVV, and missing-header paths yield only masked data in every reachable sink; no formatter dependence.
test_note: Create_order_masks_card_data_in_command in tests/Ordering.UnitTests/Application/OrdersWebApiTest.cs captures the mediated command and asserts masked PAN and CVV.
review_reason: Masks at the API boundary — strictly stronger than redacting at LoggingBehavior — consistent with the existing maskedCCNumber idiom and the code's own comment; no validation weakened.
